# Security and Privacy Requirements Quality Checklist: Installable PWA Shell

**Purpose**: Check whether the security and privacy requirements of the shell, the static site, the images, the pipeline and the iPhone test procedure are present, clear, consistent and measurable, before tasks are generated
**Created**: 2026-11-01
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md) | [contracts/](../contracts/)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

Depth: formal pre-tasks review. Audience: the reviewer of the spec and plan (the owner). References: `Spec §` is spec.md, `Research R-nn` is research.md, `Contract` is a file under contracts/, `Quickstart` is quickstart.md.

## Threat Model and Scope

- [x] CHK001 Is a threat model (assets, actors and trust boundaries for the shell, the site, the local test stack and the CI pipeline) written down, so that each requirement below traces to a stated threat? [Traceability, Gap]
- [x] CHK002 Are the security and privacy properties deliberately left to later features (sign-in, API authentication, protection of locally stored user text, the forced update on HTTP 426) listed as out of scope, each with the feature that owns it, instead of being implied by "a shell only"? [Completeness, Spec §A-001]
- [x] CHK003 Is the applicability of Brazil's data-protection law (LGPD) to the two-user app and to the public site stated, or explicitly declared out of scope? [Assumption, Gap]
- [x] CHK004 Do the response headers and the Content-Security-Policy, which exist only in contracts/http-serving.md, have a spec-level requirement or success criterion that they trace to? [Traceability, Gap, Contract http-serving §Headers]

## Browser-Side Hardening

- [x] CHK005 Is the policy's reliance on the `default-src` fallback for scripts, fonts, objects and workers intended and stated, given that no `script-src` or `object-src` is listed? [Clarity, Contract http-serving §Headers]
- [x] CHK006 Is each deliberately permissive allowance (inline styles, and `data:` and `blob:` images) justified for a shell that shows no user content, with the residual risk accepted in writing and the condition for removing it? [Assumption, Research R-16]
- [x] CHK007 Is the site's policy justified on its own (no framework injects styles there), or is "same headers as the app" a reuse by default? [Consistency, Contract http-serving §Site]
- [x] CHK008 Is the full set of required response headers justified, including why framing is controlled by `frame-ancestors` alone, what the `Permissions-Policy` list is meant to cover, and why no HSTS is sent? [Completeness, Contract http-serving §Headers]
- [x] CHK009 Is the dependency on the edge proxy for TLS, HSTS and redirection to HTTPS recorded as an assumption about the sibling stack, with the equivalent for the future cluster named as a handoff? [Dependency, Contract http-serving, Spec §A-008]
- [x] CHK010 Are requirements defined for the app being reached over plain HTTP or from an untrusted origin (no offline support, not installable, what the user sees)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK011 Is it required that production bundles ship no source maps or development-only code, and that image build arguments never carry secrets (they stay visible in image metadata)? [Completeness, Gap, Contract http-serving §Image runtime contract]
- [x] CHK012 Can "the catalogue is unreachable in production" be kept true for published images, or does it depend on release scripts that do not exist yet, given that a catalogue-enabled test build is supported? [Measurability, Spec §FR-024, Contract http-serving §Image runtime contract]

## Service Worker, Cache and Update Integrity

- [x] CHK013 Is it specified that a new version is accepted only from the app's own HTTPS origin, and is the integrity of what an update installs addressed beyond "one coherent version"? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK014 Is a recovery path defined for a faulty or malicious version that is already installed (a rollback treated as an update, a way to switch the worker off, manual removal), given that an installed app keeps its version until the user acts? [Recovery, Gap, Spec §FR-011, §FR-015]
- [x] CHK015 Is the trade-off between "never reload by itself" and delivering a security fix acknowledged, with the deferred forced update named as the mitigation and given an owner? [Assumption, Spec §FR-011, §A-001]
- [x] CHK016 Is it required, as a rule and not only as the absence of cache groups in a configuration, that the service worker never stores user-specific data or API responses, now and when later features add API calls? [Gap, Research R-02]
- [x] CHK017 Are the requirements for the storage request complete for browsers that show a permission prompt (what the user sees, what happens on dismissal, whether it is asked again)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017, Data model §StorageProtection]

## Privacy and Data Handling

- [x] CHK018 Is the statement "stores no user data" reconciled with what the shell does store (the cache of app files, the `sspc.storage.requested` flag), and is the complete list of stored items part of the requirements? [Consistency, Spec §A-001, Data model §StorageProtection]
- [x] CHK019 Is the absence of analytics, error reporting, remote fonts, remote images and any other third-party request in the **app** stated as a requirement, as it is for the site? [Gap, Spec §FR-035, §A-010]
- [x] CHK020 Is the disclosure of the version and build reference (shown on About and embedded in the public bundle) justified for a shell that anyone who can reach the address opens without signing in, and is that reachability stated as intended? [Assumption, Spec §FR-017, §FR-018]
- [x] CHK021 Do the access-log requirements conflict with FR-035's "collecting no visitor data", since the site image writes a JSON access log (client address, user agent, path) by design and no content or retention limits are stated? [Conflict, Spec §FR-035, Contract http-serving §Site]
- [x] CHK022 Are the contents, purpose and retention of the app's access log defined (the offline proof needs it; a cluster would keep it), including which fields are redacted beyond `Cookie` and `Authorization`? [Completeness, Spec §FR-037, Contract http-serving §Global options and logging]
- [x] CHK023 Is "collecting no visitor data" defined measurably (no cookies, no browser storage, no third-party requests) so that a check can assert it? [Measurability, Spec §FR-035, §A-010]
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements defined for personal data in owner-supplied images (location and device metadata removed before they ship) and for the personal names and photos shown on the public links page? [Gap, Research R-14 G7, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK025 Is it stated that the partnerships email address is intentionally public (exposure to scrapers accepted), and are the opening rules for the three outside destinations (new context, no opener access, no referrer) specified? [Assumption, Gap, Spec §FR-034]

## Container and Image Hardening

- [x] CHK026 Does the spec require the same runtime restrictions (unprivileged user, read-only filesystem, no capabilities, no privilege escalation) of the site image as of the app image? FR-030 names only the app, while the contract applies them to both. [Consistency, Spec §FR-030, §FR-031, Contract http-serving]
- [x] CHK027 Does "no added privileges" in FR-030 unambiguously mean both "all Linux capabilities removed" and "no privilege escalation", as the plan assumes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-030]
- [x] CHK028 Is the set of files each image may contain defined as an allowlist (built output only), so that the site's Dockerfile, Caddyfile and tests, and the repository's source, specs and `DESIGN.md`, are never served? [Gap, Spec §FR-031, Plan §Project Structure]
- [x] CHK029 Is pinning the base images by digest a requirement or a recommendation? The research calls it "recommended and a task". [Ambiguity, Research R-18]

Review finding for CHK026–CHK027: FR-030 now explicitly applies all four runtime restrictions to both images.

## Pipeline, Supply Chain and Secrets

- [x] CHK030 Do Story 7 scenario 6 and FR-026 ("an image with a high or critical vulnerability fails") conflict with the plan, which ignores findings that have no fix? Is the intended severity and "unfixed" rule stated in the spec? [Conflict, Spec §US7, §FR-026, Research R-18]
- [x] CHK031 Is the severity threshold for vulnerable dependencies stated in the spec (it says "known-vulnerable", the plan fails on high and critical), and is the production-only audit justified when development tools run during the image build? [Ambiguity, Spec §US7, Research R-18]
- [x] CHK032 Is there a defined way to accept or suppress a scan finding (who decides, where it is recorded, when it expires) and a time limit for fixing a high or critical advisory? [Gap, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK033 Does FR-029's "holds no deployment secrets" extend to the token's permissions, credential persistence, the pinning of third-party actions and tools, and the handling of pull requests from untrusted sources, or is untrusted-contributor handling declared out of scope for a two-person project? [Completeness, Assumption, Spec §FR-029, Research R-18]
- [x] CHK034 Is the rule "the Stitch API key is never a literal" (with the `.env*` and `*.key` ignore rules) tied to a named check that fails when it is broken? [Measurability, Contract build-and-ci §Stitch MCP configuration, Research R-21]
- [x] CHK035 Is the advisory-only nature of the gates (no branch protection on the host plan, sibling decision D-003) stated in the spec as a residual risk with its compensating control, given that FR-026 reads as if merging depended on the checks? [Assumption, Spec §FR-026, Research R-18]

## iPhone Test over the Home Network

- [x] CHK036 Are requirements defined for ending the test period (removing trust of the local certificate authority and any profile from the phone, stopping LAN exposure, clearing stored data), and for recording that this was done? Only the quickstart refers to it. [Gap, Spec §FR-036, §FR-037, Quickstart D5]
- [x] CHK037 Is "synthetic data only" (the stack is reachable from the home network while it runs) a requirement of the procedure instead of a quickstart prerequisite? [Gap, Spec §FR-036, Quickstart §Prerequisites]
- [x] CHK038 Does the verification record have limits on what it may contain, so that a committed record carries no network identifiers (LAN address, hostname), device identifiers, certificate fingerprints or client addresses from log excerpts? [Gap, Spec §FR-037, Quickstart D5]
- [x] CHK039 Is the dependency on the sibling's trust procedure pinned to a specific sibling document or version, given that the quickstart marks sibling commands "(check)" because that repository is still changing? [Dependency, Spec §FR-038, §A-007]

## Agent Tooling

- [x] CHK040 Is the coding agent's access to Stitch limited by a verifiable requirement (read-only; a tool in neither list needs approval), with the destination of downloaded Stitch files constrained and Stitch-generated content declared untrusted input that is never executed or copied? [Gap, Research R-21, Constitution §VI]

## Notes

- Items most likely to need a change to the spec or plan, not just a reviewer tick: CHK021 (site access log versus "collecting no visitor data"), CHK026 (site image restrictions missing from FR-030), CHK028 (what the site image serves), CHK030 (unfixed findings versus the spec's wording), CHK036 and CHK038 (end of the test period and the contents of the committed record).
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference

## Review findings (2026-11-01)

SEC-001–SEC-012 and the threat model in [spec.md](../spec.md), together with the updated contracts, address the checked criteria. These markers review requirements quality; implementation and owner actions remain outstanding.


The local test proxy and insecure-origin behavior are specified in SEC-001/SEC-008 and the HTTP contract. Local TLS is already available; redirects and HSTS are explicitly assigned to future hosting. These controls still require implementation and verification.

CHK012: SEC-004 and the published-image validation handoff now specify digest-based inspection and a promotion block. The workflow remains future work; this checkbox records requirements quality only.

## Spec changes after this review (agent note, 2026-11-01)

The items above were reviewed against an earlier text. Since then the spec and contracts changed in places that touch some of them. The markers are unchanged; the reviewer decides whether to re-confirm.

- CHK010: SEC-001 now says the app adds no install control and that the browser's own Add to Home Screen is outside its control (before: "not installable").
- CHK021, CHK023: A-010 now points to FR-035 and SEC-008, and the site smoke test and content check also assert that no response carries a `Set-Cookie` header.
- CHK028: the app image allowlist now lists `images/` (the About photo, from `public/images/`), and the `image-metadata` policy check covers `public/images/`.
- CHK034: the `agent-settings` check now expects one state of `.claude/settings.json`: the six read tools allowed, `generate_screen_from_text`, `edit_screens` and `apply_design_system` on `ask`, the other seven write tools denied (constitution Principle VI v2.1.0). The Stitch API key rule (never a literal) is unchanged.
